identitySignals: Agenda names 'Oakland Fund for Children and Youth' as grant funder; the City of Oakland's official page and ofcy.org describe OFCY as the City's voter-approved grantmaking program for Oakland children and youth

OFCY funds community organizations serving Oakland youth through age 21, consistent with a grant for peer restorative justice facilitation in OUSD schools and OUSD's 'Student health, support & family services' category
It is a public City program (Human Services Department), not a nonprofit or company, so no EIN or state entity registration applies
research.notes: Public agency program of the City of Oakland; no EIN, CA entity number or UEI applicable. The City's OFCY page lists '1 Frank H. Ogawa Plaza' while the OFCY contact page lists '150 Frank H. Ogawa Plaza, Suite 4216'; the latter is used.

profile.address: 150 Frank H. Ogawa Plaza, Suite 4216, Oakland, CA 94612
profile.summary: The Oakland Fund for Children and Youth (OFCY) is a City of Oakland program, created by Oakland voters in 1996 and renewed in 2009 and 2020. It gives grants to community organizations that provide services to Oakland children, youth and families from birth through age 21. It is part of the Children and Youth Services Division of the City's Human Services Department.

review.notes: OFCY is the City of Oakland grantmaking program named in the agenda as the funder of the OUSD grant application; the cited ofcy.org and City pages confirm the 1996 creation, 2009 and 2020 reauthorizations, birth-to-21 scope, Human Services Department placement, and the phone, email and address. Minor nuance: the 2020 renewal was by City Council rather than voters, but the summary wording is acceptably close.
